figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of identity-guided neural population analysis. (a) Conceptual overview. Multimodal biological features organize neurons into corresponding groups across sessions, even when exact individual neurons cannot be matched across subjects. Population dynamics are described at the level of these identity-defined groups and their interactions. (b) Identity-guided routing framework. Identity-related features are encoded to softly route neuron-level activity tokens into latent group tokens, which are processed into a population embedding. Manifold learning, stimulus classification, and behavior decoding are evaluated as separate downstream objectives.

Table 1: Behavior and stimulus decoding under direct held-out transfer across three datasets (mean ± std). Bold indicates the best result per column within each dataset. * denotes models adapted to calcium signals.
Table 2: Geometric structure of latent trajectories evaluated on held-out animals or sessions across three datasets (mean ± std). Bold indicates the best result per column.

Figure 2: Latent trajectories for two source animals (Fish 59 and Fish 63) and held-out animals across all methods. Points are colored by time within each recording. Our method preserves structured temporal trajectories in held-out animals, whereas baseline methods yield fragmented or collapsed trajectories under direct held-out transfer.
